evidence: Measurements are commonly encoded as numerical feature vectors.
Observation vectors can be arranged as rows of a data matrix.
A numerical data matrix is a matrix.
Eigenvectors identify invariant directions of a square linear transformation.
PCA directions are eigenvectors of a covariance matrix or equivalent singular-vector directions.
PCA is commonly applied to a centered numerical data matrix.
A gradient collects first partial derivatives of a scalar-valued function.
Gradient information guides many iterative optimization algorithms.
Regression parameters can be estimated by minimizing a loss function.
Neural-network parameters are commonly learned by numerical optimization.
Expectation is computed with respect to a probability distribution.
Shannon entropy quantifies uncertainty in a discrete probability distribution.
Bayes' rule updates a prior distribution using observed evidence.
A Markov transition kernel assigns next-state probability distributions.
Discrete diffusion formulations use forward and reverse Markov chains.
Continuous-time diffusion formulations can be expressed with differential equations.
Neural networks commonly parameterize learned denoising or score functions.
Compartmental epidemic models are often systems of differential equations.
Classical molecular dynamics evolves equations of motion numerically.
Probability distributions can represent measurement variability and uncertainty.
Expected values can summarize repeated uncertain measurements.
Regression design and response data are commonly represented numerically.
Many neural-network interfaces accept and return numerical vectors or tensors.
Differential equations are defined through derivatives of unknown functions.
Cross-entropy objectives are widely used when training classification networks.
